Subject: Environment activation & access matrix for Private deployment (next steps)

Hi Jamie —

Thanks again for confirming the Private deployment track. Ahead of the kickoff (target week of 2027-04-04) we need a short activation pass to validate network and access primitives. I attached a concise checklist and an access-matrix template to speed this up. Please see the high‑level prerequisites below and let me know what you can get us by EOD 2027-03-29.

High-level prerequisites (abbreviated):
- VPC/subnet CIDR(s) for Redwood egress and control plane (please include AZ mappings if relevant)
- VPN or dedicated Interconnect details (BGP ASN, local IPs, tunnel IPs), or confirmation of AWS Direct Connect/Equinix CX circuit
- CIDR(s) allowed for incoming traffic and management CIDR for bastion hosts
- Service account(s) that can be provisioned and the email address alias (we will provide minimal IAM role templates)
- KMS key ownership and requested key policy (we need an IAM principal for Redwood for envelope encryption)
- Firewall rules and approved outbound egress policy (which ports to allow/deny; see questions below)
- Time sync/NTP policy and DNS delegation plan for the Redwood FQDN(s)
- TLS certs: either ACM + private CA integration or provide cert chain for FQDNs we serve
- Audit/log forwarding target (S3/GCS/LogHub) and retention window for logs

Specific network ports for the runtime: 8600/tcp (control plane), 8443/tcp (admin API), 2379/tcp (etcd where applicable), and ephemeral ports for model serving (we provide concrete port list in the attachment).

Attachments included: redwood-private-prereqs-v2.pdf, env-access-matrix-template.xlsx, network-diagram-v1.png

Next steps:
- Jamie: fill the access matrix and attach any existing network diagrams or circuit worksheets by 2027-03-29
- Dev/Neha: we will validate KMS and IAM requirements and follow up with a short policy snippet
- Laura: schedule the kickoff once we have matrix items flagged as "ready" (aiming for week of 2027-04-04)

If anything on the list is a hard blocker, call it out in the matrix and we’ll put it on the kickoff agenda.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415 555 0124 | dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Jamie —

Quick answers inline for the network/security team: 

> 1) Port 8600 — is that the only control-plane port that needs peering?

Short answer: control plane traffic primarily uses 8600 for the control API and 8443 for admin/tls. Model serving uses a small ephemeral range (we recommend 31000-32000) for gRPC endpoints when deploying on k8s nodes behind the NLB. If you prefer a single allowed range we can push the serving ports into a contiguous range. We will document port mappings in the final checklist.

> 2) KMS key: we operate in a shared KMS account. Can Redwood accept a key you do not own if you are given Encrypt/Decrypt/grant permissions only?

Yes — Redwood supports Bring-Your-Own-KMS (BYOK) patterns. We only need a key-granting principal for envelope operations and an IAM policy that allows DescribeKey/Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey. I attached a short policy snippet you can paste into your KMS key policy (kms-policy-snippet.txt). For FIPS-labeled keys we may need to validate the cipher suites but generally it’s supported.

> 3) TLS: we prefer to terminate TLS at our NLB (internal) and pass through to your service with mTLS. Is that supported?

We support both termination at customer edge and end-to-end mTLS between the NLB and Redwood runtime. Two notes: (a) if you terminate at NLB and use mTLS internally, we’ll need certificate public keys for validation; (b) service account mapping for the mTLS cert must be included in the access matrix.

Action items from Dev:
- Provide kms-policy-snippet.txt for your security team to try (attached).
- Provide consolidated port-range table for change window planning (we’ll send by 2027-03-24).

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Infra & Integrations Lead | Redwood Inference
